- **self**: Validation and performance review of generated queries (16/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Define projection and ordering rules before scoring generated MQL. DocSpider compares executed MQL with reference SQL results, treats unordered rows as equivalent when ordering was not requested, and repairs projection or required-order errors. AptMQL-Bench instead permits extra returned fields under Soft-EX. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/research/introducing-aptmql-bench-text-to-mql-benchmark · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries · also: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/natural-language-processing/article/docspider-a-dataset-of-crossdomain-natural-language-querying-for-mongodb/1E35B1DBF843B9E0F444B595B975695A

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use explain to review performance separately from answer correctness. Inspect returned documents, scanned documents and index keys, and plan stages such as COLLSCAN and IXSCAN. A production account from Genie AI describes a correct query that examined many documents until a partial index improved it. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/code-mode-without-interpreter-agents-that-write-aggregation-pipelines

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Validate results as well as executability: AptMQL-Bench reports some models producing executable MQL about 98–99% of the time while its best evaluated model reaches 70.34% Soft-EX with external knowledge. This is a benchmark-specific result, not a production reliability guarantee. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/research/introducing-aptmql-bench-text-to-mql-benchmark · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] AptMQL-Bench defines Soft-EX as returning the same rows and matching every ground-truth field value while permitting extra fields. Extra or missing rows and incorrect values still fail; Strict-EX instead requires field-for-field equality. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/research/introducing-aptmql-bench-text-to-mql-benchmark · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] A result limit can silently undermine completeness: the Genie AI account warns that an exhaustive query reaching its limit returns a plausible subset. Review truncation and coverage before presenting generated-query results as complete. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/code-mode-without-interpreter-agents-that-write-aggregation-pipelines · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] IBM's Text-to-SQL Evaluation Toolkit combines execution accuracy, syntactic equivalence, and LLM judging with real-database execution, profiling, and per-record error analysis. It is a SQL evaluation reference; the cited publication does not establish native MQL support. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-31) — https://research.ibm.com/publications/text-to-sql-evaluation-toolkit · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] FLEX demonstrates that execution-result equality can reward incorrect SQL logic because of coincidental database contents. Ambiguous questions and imperfect reference annotations can also reject valid answers. This is SQL evidence, not a measured MQL error rate. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2409.19014v4 · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Explain bypasses the plan cache and does not populate it. Its executionTimeMillis includes planning and execution but excludes network transmission, and may differ from steady-state latency; benchmark actual application queries as well. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain/
- [statement] Read explain's nReturned, totalKeysExamined, totalDocsExamined, and execution stages together. COLLSCAN scans a collection; IXSCAN scans index keys. totalDocsExamined counts examinations rather than unique documents and can exceed the number returned. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] The First Past the Post evaluation varies predicate selectivity and compares measured candidate-plan runtimes. This supports testing generated-query performance across parameter values rather than assessing only one successful execution. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2409.16544v1 · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For find queries, cursor.explain defaults to queryPlanner. executionStats executes the winning plan to completion; allPlansExecution additionally reports partial candidate-plan statistics captured during selection. Consequently, execution-statistics review of a generated read query can incur its full execution cost. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain/ · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [statement] In Genie AI's implementation, an application handler checks permitted aggregation stages, rejects write and cross-collection stages, and prepends a workspace filter whose identifier is held outside model parameters. This is an application-specific validation pattern, not proof that aggregation pipelines are inherently read-only or tenant-safe. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/code-mode-without-interpreter-agents-that-write-aggregation-pipelines · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] Evaluate generated queries using complementary execution, structural, and semantic checks. SQL evaluation research shows that multiple valid formulations and imperfect execution-based judgments make any single metric incomplete; applying this evaluation design to MQL is a methodological inference. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2409.19014v4 · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries · also: https://research.ibm.com/publications/text-to-sql-evaluation-toolkit
- [statement] MongoDB's AptMQL-Bench conversion workflow first checks SQL-to-MQL result equivalence, then optimizes the MQL and has a reviewer confirm equivalence. This provides a concrete pattern for keeping correctness checks attached to performance rewrites. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/company/research/introducing-aptmql-bench-text-to-mql-benchmark · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] The First Past the Post study found cases where MongoDB 7.0.1 preferred an index scan despite a faster collection scan. Its experiments used synthetic two-field predicates and memory-fitting indexes; the result cautions against treating index use alone as proof of good performance and does not establish behavior of later releases. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2409.16544v1 · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
- [statement] FLEX's authors report imperfect judge agreement, evaluation limited to Spider and BIRD, additional computation costs, and reproducibility risks from proprietary model changes. LLM semantic review therefore remains supplementary evidence; its reliability for MongoDB queries was not established by this study. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2409.19014v4 · keywords: Validation and performance review of generated queries
